goal: As a SentinelGas technical sales rep, answer RFQ-2026-0041 for 38 gas detection points with a 5-tab quotation workbook (cover, area BOM with discounts and controller, 5-year TCO vs MSA S5000 and Honeywell Sensepoint XCD/Rosemount 625IR, technical compliance matrix, 5-year spares). Also write an internal memo justifying the Area 3 H2S choice, the controller spare-capacity calculation and any other deviations.
delivered: Quotation_Q-2026-CS-0041_Clearwater_Springs_WTP.xlsx: cover, BOM with H2S-300X in Area 3 and H2S-200 in Area 4, CP-32+EXP-16, a TCO tab with budgetary competitor replacement prices, a compliance matrix and a spares tab. Internal_Memo_Clearwater_Product_Selection.docx has sections (a)-(c).
what_went_wrong: The memo computed spare capacity as 10/38 = 26.3% instead of 10/48 = 20.83%, missing the tight margin, the CP-64 26/64 figure and the pre-discount cost comparison (R0). The TCO tab invents competitor replacement prices without stating a SentinelGas proxy and never flags that XCD sensor life is unspecified (R1). Memo (a) recommends H2S-300X with no list or sensor prices and no 6-unit 5-year TCO comparison (R4). The agent's own web search returned the XCD manual's per-sensor -20°C to +55°C limits and no SIL claim, yet the matrix says 'XCD -40°C to +75°C transmitter; sensor-dependent', never marks XCD partial, and calls XCD SIL 'configuration-dependent' (R6, R9).

failed_items.why: Memo §B: 'Spare capacity is 48 − 38 = 10 channels, or 10 ÷ 38 = 26.3% above the current point count'. That uses the point count as the denominator rather than installed capacity (20.83%), so the tight margin over 20% is never noted. CP-64 spare (26/64) is not computed. The subagent's 'implies >=45.6 points' framing seeded this reading (medium confidence: the RFQ wording allows it, but the conclusion that it complies is unchanged).

SentinelGas replacement counts were correct, but competitor replacement costs are invented 'budgetary' figures (MSA $700/$900/$1,100; Honeywell $600/$650) rather than a stated SentinelGas proxy. The TCO tab also never notes that XCD electrochemical sensor life is unspecified, applying a 24-month cadence silently.

Memo §A recommends H2S-300X on sensor life, TruCal/XCell and IP rating. All the needed prices were in the staged price list, yet it never cites $2,650/$395 vs $3,420/$725 or computes the 6-unit 5-year TCO ($18,270 vs $20,520), so cost is not weighed.

The step-8 web_search result (XCD technical manual) listed EC and catalytic sensors at '-20°C / -4°F 55°C / 131°F'. The matrix still writes 'XCD -40°C to +75°C transmitter; sensor-dependent' and gives XCD no Partial/Non-compliant mark against the RFQ's -29°C.

The 625IR (SIL2) and S5000 ('suitable for SIL 2') were correct, but the XCD was described as 'certification is configuration-dependent'; the retrieved XCD manual makes no SIL claim. SIL 2 was also dismissed as 'a preference' rather than treated as a differentiator.

subagent_notes: Two subagents ran. One extracted the RFQ and manager briefing (accurate; it also framed spare capacity as '>=45.6, practically >=46 points', which the root followed to the 10/38 calculation). The other extracted the price list and MSA S5000 datasheet; its pricing work supported the passing BOM, spares and cover items. The root did the competitor web searches itself.
